title: Log-canonical linear series on stable pointed curves over a field
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field] and $C/k$ a proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], nonempty connected reduced nodal curve of pure dimension one [def-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres]. Let $p_1,\ldots,p_r$ be distinct smooth $k$-points, with $r\geq0$, and put $D=\sum_i p_i$ and $M=\omega_{C/k}\otimes\mathcal O_C(D)$, using the canonical nodal adjunction line [def-trf-nodal-dualizing-datum] and divisor twist [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. On every normalized reduced irreducible component $V$ [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization], assume $2g(V)-2+b_V+m_V>0$, where $b_V$ counts ambient nodal branches and $m_V$ counts markings, and $g(V)=\dim_k H^1(V,\mathcal O_V)$ [def-pc-genus]. Then $H^i(C,M^{\otimes m})=0$ for every $i>0$ and $m\geq2$; $M^{\otimes m}$ is globally generated for $m\geq2$ (the evaluation $H^0(C,M^{\otimes m})\otimes_k\mathcal O_C\to M^{\otimes m}$ is surjective). For $m\geq3$ it is very ample: its complete linear system gives a closed immersion into the projective space of one-dimensional quotients of $H^0(C,M^{\otimes m})$ [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism]. It is also normally generated: for every $j\geq0$ the multiplication map $\operatorname{Sym}^j_k H^0(C,M^{\otimes m})\to H^0(C,M^{\otimes mj})$ is surjective. Consequently evaluation identifies $C$ with $\operatorname{Proj}_k\bigoplus_{j\geq0}H^0(C,M^{\otimes mj})$ for $m\geq3$ [def-nagata-relative-proj], with multiplication given by tensor products of sections [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures].

source.place: Section 1, Theorem 1.8 and Corollary 1.9, printed pp.170--173. This is the positive-degree stable case only, not the deletion or relative-contraction theorem. Higher cohomology above degree one vanishes on a proper curve. Local PDF WANTED; indexed primary scan read online.

proof.text: Properness includes finite type. A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $C$ Noetherian. Every reduced closed subcurve $B$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], hence also Noetherian by the same finite-type lemma. The dimension theorem [lem-sc-noetherian-cohomology-above-dimension] gives $H^i(B,F)=0$ for every quasi-coherent $F$ and $i>1$, including $B=C$.

source.place: Tag 02UZ (cohomology-proposition-vanishing-Noetherian); proper subcurves have dimension one.

proof.text: Let $V$ be the normalization of a reduced irreducible component $E$ of $C$. The structure map $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is proper, flat (over a field) and finitely presented (finite type over the Noetherian $k$), with reduced nodal geometric fibres of pure dimension one, so [lem-sfb-proper-nodal-dualizing-base-change] applies with $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $\Omega=k$: the canonical line $\omega_{C/k}$ of the statement, with its Jacobian-normalized datum, satisfies $\nu^*\omega_{C/k}\simeq\Omega^1_{V/k}(B_E)$, where $B_E$ has exactly $b_V$ distinct branch points, counting both points over a self-node. By [lem-trf-nodal-normalization-adjunction], $V$ is smooth proper connected and the normalization is an isomorphism over the smooth locus of $E$, in particular at the markings. The closed-point residue-field statement [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base] makes all branch and marked points rational. On the smooth curve $V$, [lem-sc-smooth-regular] and [lem-sc-regular-dim1-dvr] make the local ring at a closed point a DVR. Its uniformizer cuts out the point as an effective Cartier divisor; the pulled-back marking twist is therefore the divisor of the $m_V$ marked points. The formula of [sk-thm-picard-rr] gives canonical degree $2g(V)-2$, and [lem-pc-degree-base-change] gives degree $b_V+m_V$ for the rational-point divisor and its additivity with the canonical line. Thus $d_V:=\deg_V M=2g(V)-2+b_V+m_V$ is a positive integer by hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0BS6 (lemma-rr) and Tag 0AYY (varieties-lemma-degree-effective-Cartier-divisor); normalization-residue adjunction as in the cited nodal lemma.

proof.text: Fix any nonempty connected reduced union $B$ of components of $C$. It is nodal by [lem-trf-nodal-subcurve-boundary]. Let $v$ be its number of components, $e$ its number of internal nodes (self-nodes counted once), $a$ the number of nodes joining $B$ to its complement, $s$ the number of markings on $B$, and $G$ the sum of the normalized component genera. The same normalized components are smooth proper connected by Step 2. By [lem-trf-nodal-curve-normalization-euler], $\chi(B,\mathcal O_B)=v-e-G$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-reduced-algclosed-global-sections-product], $H^0(B,\mathcal O_B)=k$. Step 1 therefore identifies $h:=\dim_k H^1(B,\mathcal O_B)=1-v+e+G\geq0$.

By [lem-trf-degree-weighted-irreducible-components], degree on the reduced $B$ is the sum of its component degrees: the generic local rings are fields, of length one. Each normalized component maps birationally to that component and is an isomorphism off its self-nodes (Step 2), so [lem-per-birational-curve-degree-invariance] identifies these degrees with the $d_V$. Summing the branch counts counts every internal node twice and every boundary node once. Consequently
$$q:=\deg_B M=\sum_{V\subset B}d_V=2G-2v+2e+a+s=2h-2+a+s.$$
In particular $q\geq v\geq1$ and $q\geq2h-2$. By repeated application of [lem-trf-curve-degree-tensor-additive], $\deg_B(M^{\otimes m})=mq$ for every $m\geq0$.

The two inequalities $q\geq1$ and $q\geq2h-2$ imply the required bounds in all genera. For $h=0$, $q\geq1$ gives $2q\geq0$ and $3q\geq1$. For $h=1$, it gives $2q\geq2h$ and $3q\geq2h+1$. For $h\geq2$, $q\geq2h-2\geq h$ and $3q\geq6h-6\geq2h+1$. Thus, for every such $B$, $mq\geq2h$ for $m\geq2$ and $mq\geq2h+1$ for $m\geq3$.

source.place: Elementary integer inequalities after the subcurve degree calculation.

proof.text:
Let $Z\subset C$ be a zero-dimensional closed subscheme of length $\ell\leq1$, allowing the empty subscheme, and $m\geq2$. By [lem-pc-zero-dimensional-closed-subscheme-finite], $Z$ is affine and finite over $k$. If $H^1(C,I_Z\otimes M^{\otimes m})\ne0$, [lem-sfb-curve-ideal-h1-subcurve-obstruction] produces a connected reduced subcurve $B$. Each one-dimensional irreducible component of $B$ is an ambient component, since it is closed in the one-dimensional $C$. Any additional zero-dimensional irreducible component would be an isolated point disjoint from the one-dimensional components, contradicting connectedness. Thus $B$ is a union of ambient components and Steps 3--5 apply. Its intersection with $Z$ is defined by a quotient of the finite-dimensional algebra $\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$, so has length at most $\ell$. Steps 3--5 then give the contradiction
$$2h\leq\deg_B(M^{\otimes m})\leq2h-2+\ell\leq2h-1.$$
Thus this $H^1$ vanishes. Taking $Z=\varnothing$ gives $H^1(C,M^{\otimes m})=0$; Step 1 gives the claimed vanishing in every higher degree.

source.place: Tag 0E3E (lemma-vanishing-on-gorenstein), with the empty and length-one subschemes.

proof.text:
Let $m\geq3$ and let $Z\subset C$ be a zero-dimensional closed subscheme of length at most two, including the empty subscheme. Suppose $H^1(C,I_Z\otimes M^{\otimes m})\ne0$. Apply [lem-sfb-curve-ideal-h1-subcurve-obstruction] to obtain a nonempty reduced connected closed subcurve $B$ of dimension one. As proved in Step 6, this $B$ is a union of ambient components, so Steps 3--5 apply with $h=\dim_k H^1(B,\mathcal O_B)$. By [lem-pc-zero-dimensional-closed-subscheme-finite], $Z$ is finite affine. The closed immersion $Z\times_C B\hookrightarrow Z$ presents its coordinate algebra as a quotient of $\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$; hence its $k$-dimension is at most two. The obstruction therefore contradicts
$$2h+1\leq\deg_B(M^{\otimes m})\leq2h-2+\dim_k\Gamma(Z\times_C B,\mathcal O_{Z\times_C B})\leq2h.$$
Thus $H^1(C,I_Z\otimes M^{\otimes m})=0$, also when $Z$ is supported at a node and $I_Z$ is not invertible.

source.place: Tag 0E3E (lemma-vanishing-on-gorenstein), length-two case; no Cartier hypothesis on Z.

proof.text:
Write $L=M^{\otimes m}$. Tensoring $0\to I_Z\to\mathcal O_C\to\mathcal O_Z\to0$ with the locally free rank-one $L$ is exact by [lem-sc-ext-tensor-exact]. The global-sections functor is additive left exact by [lem-sc-global-sections-left-exact], and module sheaves have enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives]. The segment of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] is
$$H^0(C,L)\longrightarrow H^0(C,L\otimes\mathcal O_Z)\longrightarrow H^1(C,I_Z\otimes L).$$
Steps 6 and 7 make the first map surjective for length at most one if $m\geq2$, and length at most two if $m\geq3$.

Each closed point $x$ has residue field $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base]. Apply Step 8 to its reduced length-one subscheme. Some section has nonzero value in the one-dimensional fibre $L(x)$. In a local generator of $L$, its coefficient has nonzero residue and is a unit; that section therefore trivializes $L$ on a neighbourhood of $x$. The union of these neighbourhoods has closed complement with no closed point. By [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space], a nonempty closed subset would contain a closed point, so the complement is empty. These sections locally generate $L$, proving surjectivity of evaluation for $m\geq2$.

source.place: Global generation from length-one restriction and the Jacobson property over a field.

proof.text: Assume $m\geq3$. For two distinct closed points, Step 8 applied to their disjoint union supplies a section with values $(0,1)$ after trivializing the two fibres. For a nonzero tangent vector $\theta$ at $x$, the corresponding homomorphism $\mathcal O_{C,x}\to k[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ is surjective: some element of the maximal ideal has nonzero $\theta$-value. Choose an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $x$. The composite $A\to\mathcal O_{C,x}\to k[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ is still surjective, since constants and a nonzero tangent value span its target. Its kernel defines a length-two closed subscheme of $U$ supported at $x$. On $U\setminus\{x\}$ its ideal is the unit ideal, so it glues with the unit ideal on $C\setminus\{x\}$ to a closed subscheme $Z$ of $C$. Step 8 supplies a section restricting, in a local trivialization, to $\epsilon$; it vanishes at $x$ with nonzero derivative along $\theta$. Thus [lem-sc-point-tangent-separation-closed-immersion], with all global sections as $V$, applies to the proper $C$ and the invertible $L$: generation is Step 9, point separation and tangent separation were just checked. It gives a closed immersion by the complete linear system and its hyperplane pullback is $L$. The quotient interpretation and the pulled-back universal quotient in [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry] identify this morphism with the evaluation morphism into the projective space of one-dimensional quotients of $H^0(C,L)$.

source.place: Tag 0E8S (varieties-lemma-separate-points-tangent-vectors); length-two restriction argument of Tag 0E8X (lemma-tricanonical).

proof.text:
Fix $m\geq3$ and $L=M^{\otimes m}$. Step 10 makes $C$ projective. For any nonempty reduced union $B$ of components, write it as the disjoint union of its $c\geq1$ connected components $B_t$. The degree formula of Step 4 applied componentwise and $\chi$ on a finite disjoint union give
$$\deg_B L=\sum_t\deg_{B_t}L\geq\sum_t(2p_a(B_t)+1)=2p_a(B)+3c-2\geq2p_a(B)+1.$$
Here $p_a(B)=\sum_t p_a(B_t)-c+1$; this calculation also includes $B=C$. Apply [lem-sfb-nodal-numerical-section-multiplication] to the projective reduced nodal $C$ and $L$, with precisely these inequalities. It gives surjectivity of every positive-degree multiplication map in the assertion. For $j=0$, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-reduced-algclosed-global-sections-product] identifies $H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)=k$ since $C$ is nonempty and connected, and the map $\operatorname{Sym}^0_k H^0(C,L)=k\to H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)$ is the structure isomorphism.

source.place: Franciosi--Tenni, The canonical ring of a 3-connected curve, Section 4, Theorem 4.2, p.49; numerical application to L, not an assumption of stability in the cited theorem.

proof.text: Let $S=\bigoplus_{j\geq0}H^0(C,L^{\otimes j})$. Step 11 says that $S$ is generated over $S_0=k$ by $S_1$ with its actual tensor-product multiplication. The complete embedding of Step 10 identifies $L$ with the pulled-back hyperplane line, so [lem-pc-very-ample-ample] makes $L$ ample. The same embedding satisfies the polarization hypothesis of [lem-sfb-projective-polarization-section-algebra]; in particular $C_s$ is affine for each homogeneous positive-degree section $s$. Step 9 gives the positive-degree section cover required by [lem-sc-ample-proj-local-chart], whose canonical map $C\to\operatorname{Proj}S$ restricts to an isomorphism $C_s\simeq D_+(s)$. Its inverse-image identity is part of the same cited statement. The opens $D_+(s)$ with $s\in S_1$ cover $\operatorname{Proj}S$: a homogeneous prime containing $S_1$ would contain every positive-degree element by generation and thus would not be a Proj point. These local inverse maps glue uniquely on intersections, since they invert the same canonical map. Hence evaluation is an isomorphism $C\simeq\operatorname{Proj}_k S$ as asserted. The fraction formula in [lem-sc-ample-proj-canonical-map] sends a constant $a\in S_0=k$ to the same constant function on every $C_s$. Thus the canonical morphism, and its inverse, are over $k$.
